Claude Code can pull components through the shadcn MCP, and the new Field, Empty and Questionnaire components cover form UX and empty states. This is a 2025-2026 change that makes it much better than commonly believed.
gems.use_in_pool: Create a private '@pool' registry (pool card, bid row, price chip, status timeline) so all 5 developers install identical components. Use Questionnaire for seller onboarding and KYC steps, Empty for 'no pools near you yet', and tweakcn to generate the brand theme in minutes. shadcn charts cover the seller and admin dashboards.

gems.maturity_risk: Low for shadcn. tweakcn is a single-maintainer project, but you only export CSS variables from it, so lock-in is zero.

gems.name: Reanimated 4 (CSS animations and transitions syntax)
gems.what_it_is: Reanimated 4 lets you write CSS-style keyframe animations and transitions (animationName, transitionProperty) directly in React Native styles, running on Android, iOS and Web.
gems.why_gem: It is well known, but many developers still write heavy worklet code. The 4.x CSS API makes 80% of micro-interactions declarative and cheap, which suits 5 TypeScript web developers. Bluesky's production app is on Reanimated ~4.6. Latest is 4.7.0.
gems.use_in_pool: Every micro-interaction: the pool progress bar filling, the price chip pulsing when a new lower bid lands, status-timeline steps ticking, and a skeleton shimmer. Also the React Native side of the animated price ticker, since there is no maintained RN port of NumberFlow.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces the RN Animated API, Moti and hand-written worklets for simple cases.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.maturity_risk: Low. The 4.x line requires the New Architecture.

gems.name: Pulsar (react-native-pulsar) haptics SDK by Software Mansion
gems.what_it_is: A cross-platform haptics SDK with 150+ presets, a pattern composer and a realtime composer that is worklet-compatible with Reanimated. It detects each device's haptic capability and falls back automatically. Pulsar Studio designs custom haptics, including from Lottie or audio.
gems.why_gem: It was created in October 2025 and is barely known (458 stars), yet it already has about 104k weekly downloads. The alternative, expo-haptics, offers only a handful of basic impacts. Pulsar's capability fallback matters for cheap Android phones with poor vibration motors.
gems.use_in_pool: Tactile confirmation at trust moments: a 'coin drop' when the Wave Drop refund lands, a firm tick when the delivery code is verified, and a light tap when a new bid arrives. It makes the demo feel premium without extra UI.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces expo-haptics and react-native-haptic-feedback.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT (SDK). Pulsar Studio pricing not verified.
gems.activity_evidence: 458 stars; react-native-pulsar 1.7.0 (npm modified 2026-08-11); repo pushed 2026-09-21; about 104k weekly downloads.
gems.maturity_risk: Young. Requires the New Architecture and RN 0.71+. Advanced effects need Android API 30+ (envelopes API 36+).

gems.name: NumberFlow (@number-flow/react)
gems.what_it_is: A dependency-free, accessible animated-number component. Digits roll smoothly when the value changes. It takes Intl.NumberFormat options and locales and respects reduced motion by default.
gems.why_gem: For the single most important POOL moment, the price dropping as the pool grows, it gives Robinhood-style digit rolling in one component. It is correct with Intl formatting, so '₹1,24,999' in en-IN grouping and '$1,249.99' both work. About 2.1M weekly downloads, yet rarely mentioned in 'best libraries' lists.
gems.use_in_pool: The web and PWA pool page: live per-buyer price, the 'you save' amount and the member count. On React Native, replicate it with Reanimated, because the only RN port (rn-number-flow 0.1.6) has not been updated since 2024-11.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces hand-rolled counters and react-countup.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: 7,718 stars; number-flow@0.6.2 released 2026-07-18; about 2.1M weekly npm downloads.
gems.maturity_risk: Web only (React, Vue, Svelte); there is no maintained React Native version. Still on 0.x.

gems.name: react-native-fast-confetti (Skia Atlas)
gems.what_it_is: A confetti and particle library rendered with @shopify/react-native-skia's Atlas API (batched drawing), animated with Reanimated. It offers Confetti, ContinuousConfetti, PIConfetti (burst) and CannonConfetti, supports custom SVG or image flakes, and respects reduce-motion.
gems.why_gem: Because particles are drawn in one Skia batch instead of hundreds of Views, it is the only realistic way to do celebration effects on low-end Android without jank. Its 'fastest' claim is not benchmarked, but the architecture is sound.
gems.use_in_pool: A small, tasteful burst when a pool closes successfully or a Wave Drop refund is confirmed. You can use rupee- or coin-shaped flakes. Show it once, never in a loop.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces react-native-confetti-cannon (View-based) and Lottie confetti files.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: 575 stars; v2.0.2 released 2026-07-17; last push 2026-08-26.
gems.maturity_risk: Small single-maintainer project. v2 needs RN 0.79+, React 19 and Skia 2. The effect is non-critical, so the risk is acceptable.

gems.name: json-render (Vercel Labs), guardrailed generative UI
gems.what_it_is: A framework in which an LLM outputs JSON that can only use components and actions from a catalog you define (props validated with Zod), and the result renders progressively while streaming. It has a React Native package (@json-render/react-native, 25+ standard components).
gems.why_gem: It was created in January 2026 and has 18.4k stars, but is still unknown outside AI-frontend circles. It directly enforces POOL's rule that 'AI helps, never invents': the model cannot produce a component, field or action you did not whitelist. So an AI answer can never show a fake price or a fake seller badge.
gems.use_in_pool: Product identification results after a buyer pastes a link. The AI can only fill a 'ProductMatchCard', 'SpecTable' and 'ConfidenceNote' with Zod-typed fields, plus an 'Ask buyer to confirm' action. The same catalog renders on web and React Native.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a safe generative-UI layer. It replaces free-form markdown or chat output for AI answers.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free
gems.activity_evidence: 18,429 stars; created 2026-01-14; @json-render/core and react-native 0.21.0 published 2026-09-18; last push 2026-09-25.
gems.maturity_risk: Pre-1.0 (0.21) from Vercel Labs, which is experimental and not a product, so expect breaking changes. Pin the version.

gems.name: Google Stitch plus stitch-skills (MCP design-to-code for Claude Code)
gems.what_it_is: A Google Labs AI design canvas: prompts or screenshots become multi-screen UI. The official stitch-skills repo (Apache-2.0) adds agent skills for Claude Code and Cursor, including react-components, react-native, shadcn-ui and design-md, that pull designs through the Stitch MCP server into code.
gems.why_gem: Most founders compare v0 and Lovable. Stitch plus MCP is less known, and it is the one route where the design tool feeds Claude Code directly in the team's existing workflow, with a dedicated React Native conversion skill. The skills repo has 8.4k stars since January 2026.
gems.use_in_pool: Explore 5-10 visual directions for the core buyer flow (paste link, match, pool, bids, pay, code) in hours. Export a DESIGN.md with tokens, then have Claude Code turn it into Uniwind and Reusables components. Treat the output as a starting scaffold, not shipped code.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a fast design-exploration step. Partly replaces Figma-first design and v0.
gems.license_or_pricing: stitch-skills Apache-2.0. Stitch itself was reported as free (Google Labs); exact limits not verified.
gems.activity_evidence: stitch-skills 8,400 stars, created 2026-01-16, last push 2026-08-17. Review sites report a March 2026 canvas update.
gems.maturity_risk: A Google Labs experiment, so it could change or be shut down. The exported code needs cleanup. India availability and quotas are not verified.

gems.name: mapcn (web) plus MapLibre React Native v11 on OpenFreeMap tiles
gems.what_it_is: mapcn provides shadcn-style React map components on MapLibre GL: markers, popups, routes and controls, installed through the shadcn CLI. MapLibre RN v11 is the maintained open-source native map SDK. OpenFreeMap serves free vector tiles with no API key, no request limits and commercial use allowed.
gems.why_gem: mapcn launched in December 2025 and already has 12.2k stars. Together these give Swiggy-style map UI with zero per-load map bills and no Google Maps key, and styles you fully control (on-brand, uncluttered). Watch out: mapcn's default CARTO basemap needs an enterprise licence for commercial use, so point it at OpenFreeMap or self-hosted tiles.
gems.use_in_pool: 'Pools near you' map, the seller pickup-point pin, and the delivery-proof location on the tracking timeline, on both web and the RN app.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Google Maps SDK and Mapbox on the display side. Geocoding and routing still need a separate provider.
gems.license_or_pricing: mapcn MIT; MapLibre RN MIT; OpenFreeMap free, donation-funded (repo licence shown as NOASSERTION on GitHub).
gems.activity_evidence: mapcn 12,227 stars (created 2025-12-28, pushed 2026-09-06). MapLibre RN 666 stars, v11.4.0 released 2026-09-19. OpenFreeMap 6,106 stars, pushed 2026-09-13.
gems.maturity_risk: The OpenFreeMap public instance runs on donations with no SLA; self-host or keep a paid fallback (MapTiler or Stadia) for production. MapLibre RN has a small maintainer team.

gems.name: Lingui v6 (compile-time i18n)
gems.what_it_is: An ICU MessageFormat i18n library with compile-time macros: you write <Trans>Join pool</Trans> in code and the extractor builds PO catalogs. Plurals use Intl.PluralRules. v6.0 shipped 2026-04-22 (ESM-only, fewer dependencies, typed message IDs in 6.2); latest is 6.8.0.
gems.why_gem: Most teams default to i18next. Bluesky, a top consumer app on Expo 57 and RN 0.86, uses Lingui for its React Native app. Messages stay readable in source, translators work in standard PO files, and bundles stay small, which matters on low-end Android.
gems.use_in_pool: Telugu, Hindi and English UI strings with correct plurals ('1 buyer joined' vs '5 buyers joined'), one source of truth for web and app, and PO files a Telugu or Hindi translator can edit without code.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces i18next and react-intl.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: 5,901 stars; v6.8.0 released 2026-09-23; last push 2026-09-29. Used in bluesky-social/social-app (Lingui ^5.9).
gems.maturity_risk: v6 is ESM-only, so check the Metro and Next config. The macros need a Babel or SWC plugin.

gems.name: react-native-keyboard-controller
gems.what_it_is: Keyboard handling for React Native that works the same on Android and iOS: frame-by-frame keyboard animations, KeyboardAwareScrollView, a KeyboardToolbar with next/previous field buttons, and interactive dismiss.
gems.why_gem: It is the unglamorous difference between 'feels cheap' and 'feels premium' in forms on Android, where the built-in KeyboardAvoidingView is famously broken. Bluesky ships it, and it has about 2.8M weekly downloads, yet it rarely appears in 'UI library' lists.
gems.use_in_pool: Every form: link paste, address entry, seller bid entry, and OTP or delivery-code entry. Inputs never hide behind the keyboard on cheap Android phones, and a next/done toolbar speeds up entry.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces KeyboardAvoidingView and react-native-keyboard-aware-scroll-view.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: 3,737 stars; 1.22.6 released 2026-09-29; about 2.8M weekly npm downloads.
gems.maturity_risk: Low. Needs a development build (native module).

gems.name: Anek Telugu, Devanagari and Latin plus Noto Sans Telugu variable fonts (via Fontsource or expo-font)
gems.what_it_is: Anek is a variable multi-script family by Ek Type (Mumbai) covering 9 Indian scripts plus Latin, designed to match across scripts. Anek Telugu has a weight axis of 100-800 and a width axis of 75-125. Noto Sans Telugu variable has weight 100-900 and width 62.5-100. Both are OFL-1.1 and packaged on npm by Fontsource (5.3.0).
gems.why_gem: Most apps render Telugu in whatever system fallback font the phone has, so English and Telugu text look mismatched. Anek gives one visually consistent voice across Telugu, Hindi and English. The width axis lets long Telugu words fit narrow buttons without truncation.
gems.use_in_pool: Use Anek for headings, prices and buttons, where it looks best at large sizes and short text, and Noto Sans Telugu or Devanagari for body text. Web loads per-script subsets through unicode-range. The app bundles only the needed weights through expo-font.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces system-fallback Indic rendering and mismatched Latin/Indic font pairs.
gems.license_or_pricing: OFL-1.1, free
gems.activity_evidence: Google Fonts versions updated 2025-09-08 (Fontsource metadata); @fontsource-variable/anek-telugu and noto-sans-telugu 5.3.0 published 2026-07-19. The EkType repo has 76 stars (fonts are stable, last push 2022).
gems.maturity_risk: Anek is designed mainly for display sizes, so do not use it for long body text. Bundling several variable Indic fonts adds APK size; measure it.

gems.name: WhatsApp Flows (native multi-screen forms inside WhatsApp)
gems.what_it_is: Meta's framework for structured multi-screen UI rendered natively inside a WhatsApp chat: text inputs, dropdowns, date pickers, chips, PhotoPicker and an image carousel (Flow JSON 7.1). Flow JSON 7.3 and Data API 4.0 are current, and Flows work on WhatsApp Web since December 2025.
gems.why_gem: For a WhatsApp-first India product, this is a UI surface most web teams ignore. A buyer can join a pool, pick a closing time or pickup slot, or confirm an address without leaving WhatsApp or loading a web page on a slow phone.
gems.use_in_pool: 'Join this pool' Flow (quantity, pickup slot, language), 'Pool closed, accept or walk away' Flow, and seller 'submit bid' Flow for meat shops and dealers who will not install an app. Payment still goes through the PA link; the Flow does not handle money.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a chat-native UI channel. Replaces 'tap this link to open the web app' for simple steps.
gems.license_or_pricing: Free to build. Messages follow WhatsApp Business Platform per-message pricing through the founder's BSP or Cloud API account.
gems.activity_evidence: Official changelog entries in June, July, September and November 2025. No 2026 entries were visible on the changelog page today.
gems.maturity_risk: It needs an approved WhatsApp Business account, which the founder must create. The component set is limited, the endpoint needs encryption (Data API 4.0 signatures), and UI control is less than on the web.

gems.name: TrueSheet (react-native-true-sheet v3)
gems.what_it_is: Truly native bottom sheets: Android BottomSheetBehavior and iOS UISheetPresentationController. Features include detents, footer, automatic keyboard handling, tablet side sheets, first-class Reanimated support and web support. Requires the New Architecture.
gems.why_gem: Everyone defaults to @gorhom/bottom-sheet, which is JavaScript-driven and whose last release was May 2026. TrueSheet uses the OS's own sheet, so it behaves exactly as users expect and costs less on low-end Android. It is updated almost weekly (v3.11.16, 2026-09-27).
gems.use_in_pool: The core decision sheets: bid details, 'accept this price or walk away', the payment summary before handing off to the PA checkout, and the delivery-code reveal.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces @gorhom/bottom-sheet.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.maturity_risk: Single main maintainer. v3 needs RN 0.81+ with Fabric, and v4 is in beta with RN 0.82+. @expo/ui BottomSheet is an alternative if TrueSheet stalls.

gems.name: React Bits (animated React components)
gems.what_it_is: A large collection of animated text, background and interaction components for React on the web: split text, count-up, magnet buttons, animated lists and more. Available in TypeScript and Tailwind variants.
gems.why_gem: It was the #1 rising React project of 2025 (+32.8k stars) and now has 48k stars, but it is still seen as 'portfolio candy'. Used sparingly, it gives the investor landing page and the demo web app a crafted feel in hours.
gems.use_in_pool: Investor and marketing landing page only: hero text reveal, animated savings counter, 'how a pool works' scroll story. Keep it out of the core buyer flow for performance and simplicity.
gems.replaces_or_adds: An alternative to Magic UI and Aceternity for landing-page motion.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT plus Commons Clause (GitHub shows NOASSERTION). Commercial use inside the product is allowed; reselling or redistributing the components is not.

gems.maturity_risk: Not an OSI-approved licence, so have legal glance at it. Heavy effects can hurt Core Web Vitals on cheap phones. Web only.

gems.name: Rive new React Native runtime (@rive-app/react-native, Nitro-based)
gems.what_it_is: Rive's rewritten React Native runtime (0.x, Nitro modules) for interactive state-machine animations with data binding. The .riv files are small and their animation states can be driven by app data.
gems.why_gem: Compared with Lottie, a Rive mascot or pool 'fill' illustration can react live to data (members joined, price tier) instead of playing a fixed clip. The new runtime is very active (v0.5.0 released 2026-09-29) but barely known (154 stars).
gems.use_in_pool: One hero animation: the pool 'filling up' as buyers join, with state changes when a price tier unlocks. Only after the core flow is done.
gems.replaces_or_adds: An alternative to lottie-react-native for interactive illustrations.
gems.license_or_pricing: Runtime MIT. The Rive editor's Free plan cannot export .riv files; export needs Cadet at $9/seat/month (max 3 seats) or higher.
gems.activity_evidence: rive-nitro-react-native 154 stars, v0.5.0 released 2026-09-29. The legacy rive-react-native has 784 stars (v9.8.5, 2026-07-17).
gems.maturity_risk: The new runtime is pre-1.0. Export costs money. Heavy animations on low-end Android need testing. Nice-to-have, not core.

gems.name: Expo SDK 57 (SDK 58 beta), used as one universal codebase for Android, iOS and web
gems.what_it_is: React Native framework. In 2025-2026 the New Architecture became mandatory (from SDK 55), Hermes v1 became opt-in, and SDK 58 beta (2026-09-15) ships RN 0.88 RC, async routes on web by default, about 2x faster Android builds, expo-widgets and @expo/agent-cli.
gems.why_gem: This is the obvious choice, and it is included because it is much stronger than its 2023 reputation. Expo Router now emits a real web or PWA build from the same TypeScript screens. The whole team can build Android on Windows machines, and iOS is built in the cloud through EAS. SDK 58 cut Android build time from about 80s to about 39s (Expo changelog). A 5-person TS team gets one codebase for the Android Play app, the US iPhone app and the WhatsApp-linked web PWA.
gems.use_in_pool: One codebase covering the buyer app (paste link, join or start pool, pay, delivery code), the seller bid console and the web PWA that WhatsApp links open into.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces separate PWA plus native codebases, and Flutter (which is not TypeScript).
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT (expo 57.0.26 on npm). EAS Build and Update have a free tier; paid tiers are usage-based.
gems.maturity_risk: Low for SDK 57. SDK 58 is still beta, so pin to 57 for the pitches. Hermes v1 is not confirmed as the default, so test it on a 2-3GB RAM Android before enabling it.

gems.name: hot-updater (self-hosted OTA, CodePush replacement)
gems.what_it_is: Self-hostable OTA updates for React Native and Expo, with plugins for Supabase, Cloudflare R2/D1, AWS S3 and Firebase. It includes a web console, rollback, and bsdiff binary patches for smaller downloads.
gems.why_gem: Microsoft CodePush is retired. hot-updater is little known outside Korea and Japan, yet it ships releases every week. Its bsdiff delta patches matter for Indian users on prepaid data with low-end phones, because they download a diff instead of a full JS bundle. Storage stays in your own bucket, so there are no per-MAU EAS Update costs.
gems.use_in_pool: Push fixes to the pitch demo build during investor weeks without Play or App Store review, and ship small delta updates to buyers' phones.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces EAS Update (paid per MAU at scale) and the retired CodePush.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT (LICENSE file; GitHub shows NOASSERTION only because of formatting). Free; you pay only your storage and CDN.
gems.maturity_risk: Medium: 1.0 is still at release candidate and the project depends on a small maintainer team. Keep EAS Update as the fallback.

gems.name: xprem (formerly expo-open-ota)
gems.what_it_is: Self-hosted server for the official Expo Updates protocol. It adds a multi-app dashboard, progressive rollouts, instant rollbacks, and per-update crash and metric data through expo-observe.
gems.why_gem: It speaks the stock expo-updates protocol, so there is no custom native SDK. You keep Expo's own client and swap the server. That is a lower-lock-in alternative to hot-updater if the team wants to stay 100% on Expo primitives.
gems.use_in_pool: The same OTA role as hot-updater. Choose one of the two after a 1-day spike.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces the EAS Update hosted service.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT for everything outside the ee/ directories, which fall under the Mercure Enterprise licence. Self-hosted on your own bucket and CDN.
gems.activity_evidence: 646 stars. v3.2.5 released 2026-09-26. Created 2025-01.
gems.maturity_risk: Medium: the open-core split (ee/) could move features behind a paywall.

gems.name: Zero by Rocicorp (@rocicorp/zero)
gems.what_it_is: Query-driven sync engine. A Postgres server syncs the data each screen needs into a local client store, giving instant UI and optimistic writes. React Native is officially supported through expo-sqlite (IndexedDB on web) or op-sqlite.
gems.why_gem: In 2024 Zero was alpha. It is now at 1.9.0 on npm with 1.11 canaries, and it has first-party Expo support. Live pool counts, bid updates and buyer-joined events show up instantly without a hand-built websocket layer, and the same code works in the web PWA.
gems.use_in_pool: Live pool state: member count, countdown to the buyer-chosen close, bids arriving and Wave Drop price. It stays usable on flaky 4G and reconciles when back online.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces a hand-rolled REST, polling and websocket setup, and Firebase/Firestore.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0. Self-host free on your own Postgres.
gems.activity_evidence: rocicorp/mono has 3,397 stars and was pushed 2026-09-30. npm @rocicorp/zero 1.9.0 modified 2026-09-30.
gems.maturity_risk: Medium. Money state such as payments and escrow must stay server-authoritative in Postgres, never client-optimistic. op-sqlite needs a dev build, not Expo Go.

gems.name: PowerSync
gems.what_it_is: Postgres/MongoDB/MySQL to SQLite sync for React Native and web, with Sync Streams for partial sync.
gems.why_gem: It is the more battle-tested alternative to Zero for true offline use, such as a seller at a meat shop with no signal who still has to verify a pickup code. It now has a self-hostable Open Edition.
gems.use_in_pool: Offline-capable seller app: today's orders, delivery or pickup codes to verify, bid drafts. It syncs when back online.
gems.replaces_or_adds: The same role as Zero; pick one.
gems.license_or_pricing: SDKs are Apache-2.0. Cloud Free covers 2GB synced/month and 50 peak clients, but free projects are deactivated after 1 week of inactivity. Pro starts at $49/month. The self-hosted Open Edition is free and source-available.
gems.activity_evidence: powersync-js has 726 stars. @powersync/web 2.4.1 released 2026-09-23. @powersync/react-native 2.3.0.
gems.maturity_risk: Low-medium. Do not leave the pitch demo on a free project that auto-deactivates.

gems.name: react-native-vision-camera v5 (Nitro-based)
gems.what_it_is: Camera library for React Native, rebuilt in v5 on Nitro Modules. It includes a barcode scanner (it can also scan static images), GPU resizing and multi-camera support.

gems.name: UPI Reserve Pay (formerly SBMD: Single Block, Multiple Debit)
gems.what_it_is: NPCI UPI capability. The buyer blocks an amount once with a UPI PIN, and the merchant debits it fully or partly one or more times. Unused funds are released at expiry or on manual release. The limit is ₹10,000 and validity is up to 90 days.
gems.why_gem: It maps closely to POOL: block the buyer's maximum at join, debit only the final Wave Drop price at close, and release the rest. That avoids 'charge, then partially refund', and the money stays in the buyer's own account until the pool closes. Cashfree and Pine Labs expose it via API.
gems.use_in_pool: India pool join: block up to the pool's max price, debit the final price at close, release the remainder. Good for meat and grocery pools under ₹10k.
gems.replaces_or_adds: An alternative to charging upfront and then refunding the Wave Drop, for tickets under ₹10k.
gems.license_or_pricing: PG pricing; must be enabled by the Cashfree account manager.
gems.activity_evidence: Cashfree and Pine Labs docs live. Supported UPI apps: Paytm, Navi, BHIM (PhonePe and Google Pay listed as 'coming soon' by Pine Labs).
gems.maturity_risk: High. The ₹10k cap is low, most users are on PhonePe and GPay, which are not yet supported, and it needs PG enablement. The RBI and regulatory fit for a marketplace hold must be checked with the PA.

gems.name: UPI Reserve Pay (NPCI Single-Block-Multi-Debit, SBMD) through Cashfree Subscriptions sandbox (also on Razorpay and Pine Labs)
gems.what_it_is: A UPI mandate type launched at GFF Oct 2025 (SBMD renamed 'UPI Reserve Pay'). The buyer blocks up to a limit once with their UPI PIN. The merchant can then debit one or more exact amounts later without asking again, and can release whatever is unused. Razorpay documents a maximum block of Rs 10,000, token validity of up to 90 days, and multiple debits until the block is used up or the token expires. Cashfree exposes it through its Subscription API: category 'SBMD', payment_type AUTH, then CHARGE, then refund, then CANCEL to unblock. Sandbox endpoints are documented (sandbox.cashfree.com/pg/subscriptions).
gems.why_gem: It turns POOL's hardest money moment into a native UPI feature. The buyer reserves the pool's worst-case price when joining. At close, POOL debits only the final Wave Drop price. The buyer never pays and then waits for a partial refund, which cuts refund traffic, reconciliation work and 'where is my refund' tickets. Most teams still build 'pay in full, then refund the difference'. This was re-verified today in live Razorpay and Cashfree docs, including the Cashfree sandbox URL.
gems.use_in_pool: India buyer flow: join pool, then block the max price through a UPI intent. At pool close, one CHARGE for the actual per-buyer price. If the buyer walks away or the pool fails, CANCEL/unblock. The debit still settles through the PA's split/hold, so the seller gets money only after the delivery code. For amounts above Rs 10,000 (appliances), fall back to a normal PA payment with a hold plus a partial refund.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces 'full capture + Wave Drop partial refund' for India orders up to Rs 10,000, and complements the US Stripe manual-capture/extended-authorization pattern.
gems.license_or_pricing: Commercial PA product. Priced under the PA's normal UPI/subscription pricing, which is not published for SBMD specifically. Sandbox is free with test keys.
gems.activity_evidence: Launched at Global Fintech Fest Oct 2025 (RBI/NPCI). Live docs today on Cashfree (API version 2025-01-01), Razorpay (limits table and supported credit-card issuers: ICICI, Axis, PNB, Canara, Union and others) and Pine Labs.
gems.maturity_risk: Medium. The Rs 10,000 cap excludes high-value pools. Razorpay says the business category must support SBMD, so POOL's MCC must be confirmed with the PA. Some UPI apps and issuers may not support it yet. Related regulation (verified, pending): the Aug 2026 bill removed the legal ban on UPI MDR, with up to about 0.4% discussed for payments above Rs 2,000 to large merchants (about Rs 1.5 cr+ turnover), but an NPCI-led committee has not fixed a rate. RBI's PA Master Direction of 15 Sep 2025 includes marketplaces in the merchant definition and routes Delivery-versus-Payment funds through the PA escrow, which supports POOL's 'hold until delivery code' design.

gems.name: Borzo Business API (hyperlocal courier, public sandbox, multi-stop orders with proof photos)
gems.what_it_is: A REST API for same-day intracity delivery. Sandbox: https://robotapitest-in.borzodelivery.com/api/business/1.8 (self-serve test registration at apitest.borzodelivery.com). Methods: calculate-order, create-order with up to 99 points, cancel-order, courier info and live location, and webhooks for order and delivery changes. Fields include is_route_optimizer_enabled, place_photo_url, sign_photo_url, recipient_full_name, taking_amount (cash collection), insurance_amount and vehicle_type_id. Hyderabad is among the 25 Indian service areas listed.
gems.why_gem: Porter's API key comes only through a relationship manager. Shiprocket Quick and Pidge have no public API docs I could find. Borzo lets 5 developers integrate against a real sandbox this week. Its multi-point, route-optimised order fits a pool: one seller pickup, then N buyer drops in one trip. It also returns photo and signature proof per point.
gems.use_in_pool: When a meat-shop or dealer pool closes, POOL creates one Borzo order: pickup at the seller, then each buyer's drop, with route optimisation on. Webhooks feed POOL's proof-based tracking timeline, and the per-point photo and signature URLs become evidence next to POOL's own delivery-code check. calculate-order shows buyers an honest delivery cost per head before they accept a bid.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a real, testable delivery leg. Replaces the choice between hand-waving 'seller delivers' and waiting on Porter's RM-issued keys.
gems.license_or_pricing: Commercial. Priced per order, shown by calculate-order; no public rate card was checked. The sandbox is free.
gems.activity_evidence: API version 1.8 docs are live today. Press coverage says India is about 78% of Borzo's deliveries and that it raised about $60M (Mubadla, VNV Global) and plans an HQ move to Mumbai. The exact dates of those press items are not pinned down.
gems.maturity_risk: Medium. Courier quality varies by city. Keep a thin delivery-provider interface so Porter or ONDC logistics can be swapped in. Check the sandbox's behaviour for Hyderabad coordinates on day 1.

gems.name: Cashfree Secure ID: KYB and KYC verification suite for seller onboarding
gems.what_it_is: Verification APIs with sandbox and production environments and webhooks. It covers GSTIN verification (legal name, status, taxpayer type, registration date), PAN (standard and OCR), PAN-to-GSTIN, CIN, Udyam, and bank account verification (penny drop) with AI Name Match tuned for Indian names. It also has DigiLocker consent-based KYC (Aadhaar, PAN, DL) with automatic Aadhaar masking, face match and liveness, vehicle RC and DL checks, and geocoding and reverse geocoding.
gems.why_gem: If POOL's India PA is Cashfree (SBMD plus split settlement), seller verification comes from the same vendor, dashboard and sandbox, with no separate KYC vendor contract for the prototype. Name Match links 'the GSTIN legal name' to 'the bank account holder name', which is exactly the check that stops fake dealers. One anti-hype finding verified in Cashfree's docs: reverse penny drop (seller pays Rs 1 by UPI) is restricted by RBI to specific MCCs (NBFC collections, mutual funds, brokers, insurance) and is not permitted for e-commerce. POOL must use forward penny drop.
gems.use_in_pool: The 'Verified seller' badge is backed by real checks. The flow is GSTIN, then PAN-to-GSTIN match, then penny drop to the settlement account with Name Match against the GST legal name, then Udyam (optional). DigiLocker KYC covers the proprietor, with Aadhaar masked before storage. Each check result is stored with a timestamp and shown to buyers as 'GST verified on <date>'.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces manual document uploads and eyeballing, and avoids a separate KYC vendor (Sandbox.co.in from the earlier run remains the alternative if the PA is Razorpay).
gems.license_or_pricing: Commercial. Cashfree does not publish a Secure ID rate card; pricing is custom via sales. Sandbox needs IP whitelisting even for testing.
gems.activity_evidence: Live docs index (llms.txt) today lists all of the endpoints above, including Know Your Business, Udyam and Name Match.
gems.maturity_risk: Low technically. The commercial risk is unpublished pricing. DPDP Rules 2025 (notified 13 Nov 2025): the Consent Manager framework starts 13 Nov 2026 and full compliance is due 13 May 2027. POOL needs purpose-limited consent text and retention rules for these KYC artefacts.

gems.name: DIGIPIN (India Post open digital address grid)
gems.what_it_is: India Post's national geocoded addressing grid, built with IIT Hyderabad and NRSC (ISRO). It assigns a 10-character alphanumeric code to a grid cell of about 4 m x 4 m, derived from latitude and longitude. The official repo holds a small Node.js encoder/decoder, a public API server and a swagger.yaml.
gems.why_gem: Indian addresses are the silent killer of hyperlocal delivery ('near Hanuman temple, 2nd lane'). DIGIPIN is a free, deterministic and offline-computable code. MapmyIndia (Mappls) integrated it in July 2025, and it needs no vendor. Most teams have never heard of it or think it is just a government portal.
gems.use_in_pool: Every pickup point, meat shop and buyer drop gets a DIGIPIN, computed client-side from GPS on low-end Android with no network call. It is shown in the Telugu, Hindi or English address card and put in WhatsApp messages and the Borzo order note. Buyers can share 'my DIGIPIN' instead of typing an address. Use it for pool radius checks (for example, only buyers within X km of the shop).
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a precise address key on top of free-text addresses and PIN codes. Complements whichever geocoder is used (Ola Maps or Google).
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0 per the LICENSE file in INDIAPOST-gov/digipin (GitHub's API shows NOASSERTION). Free.
gems.activity_evidence: INDIAPOST-gov/digipin: 106 stars, created 14 Nov 2025, last push 29 May 2026. The original CEPT-VZG/digipin has 414 stars (Apr 2025). Several npm ports exist (digipinjs 1.3.0, @pranamphd/digipin 0.1.4 on 13 Sep 2026).
gems.maturity_risk: Low for encode/decode, which is a pure function. Port the roughly 50-line algorithm into our TS package from the official repo rather than depending on a third-party npm port of unknown quality. Adoption by couriers is still early, so always keep lat/long alongside.

gems.name: Ola Maps (Krutrim) Maps APIs, India-first maps and geocoding
gems.what_it_is: An Indian map platform with geocoding, reverse geocoding, autocomplete, directions, distance matrix, static maps and tiles. Official pricing today: 100,000 API calls per month free across all products. Tier 2 (100K to 5M) costs Rs 0.099 per geocode or direction, Rs 0.056 per autocomplete and Rs 0.040 per static map. Prepaid credits apply from 1 Sep 2026.
gems.why_gem: Rupee pricing, a free tier that covers a whole prototype and pilot, and India-specific POI and address data. This corrects a common error: many 2026 third-party pages still quote a '500K free' or '5M free' tier, but the official page now says 100K per month with prepaid credits from 1 Sep 2026.

gems.name: Bolna (YC F25): Indian voice-agent orchestration, open source plus hosted
gems.what_it_is: A voice-AI orchestration platform built for Indian enterprises. It supports 10+ Indian languages including Telugu, Hindi and Hinglish, uses Twilio, Plivo or Vobiz telephony, and supports bring-your-own LLM, ASR and TTS keys. An MIT open-source core plus a hosted Agent Studio.
gems.why_gem: Many of POOL's real sellers (meat-shop owners, small dealers) will not open an app, but they answer the phone. Bolna is a young YC company (F25) focused on India. It has a public per-minute price, a free credit, and an MIT core that can be self-hosted later. It is less known than US voice platforms, which handle Telugu poorly.
gems.use_in_pool: When a pool closes, POOL places an outbound Telugu call to eligible sellers: 'Pool of 40 x 1 kg chicken curry cut, Kukatpally, pickup 7 pm. Your price per kg?' The spoken bid is captured as structured data and followed by a WhatsApp message the seller must tap to confirm, because a voice answer is never the binding bid. It can also make reminder calls to buyers who haven't completed a UPI block.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a voice channel for low-digital sellers. Replaces manual calling by ops staff.

gems.name: Attestr: FSSAI licence check API plus continuous business monitoring
gems.what_it_is: An Indian KYB/verification API vendor. The FSSAI Licence Check API takes a 14-digit FSSAI number (plus an optional fetchProducts flag). It returns licence status (for example 'License Issued'), business name, registered address and pincode, State or Central category, state, and the licensed product list with nature of business. The homepage also advertises ongoing monitoring alerts such as 'FSSAI licence nearing expiry', 'Udyam / MSME status changed' and 'New court case filed against the entity'.
gems.why_gem: Cashfree Secure ID has no FSSAI endpoint, but FSSAI is the licence that matters for POOL's meat-shop sellers. Attestr covers it, and its monitoring means a seller who was verified in March and whose licence lapses in September loses the 'Verified' badge automatically. Most marketplaces verify once and never re-check.
gems.use_in_pool: During meat-shop onboarding, verify the FSSAI licence and check that the licensed product categories cover meat, and that the address matches the shop's DIGIPIN area. Subscribe the seller to monitoring. On an expiry or status-change alert, pause them from bidding and send a Telugu WhatsApp nudge to renew.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds food-licence verification and re-verification. It replaces manual FoSCoS portal lookups and scrapers.
gems.license_or_pricing: Commercial. Pricing not published ('create a free account' or 'talk to us').
gems.activity_evidence: Docs page is live today. The homepage lists monitoring features and ISO 27001:2022 (valid to Sep 2027) and ISO 9001 certifications. No GitHub or star metric applies.
gems.maturity_risk: Medium. Sandbox availability and pricing are unknown. The docs note an in-progress DPDP consent transition. Gridlines and Surepass offer FSSAI APIs too if terms don't work.

gems.name: Aadhaar App verifiable credentials through UIDAI OVSE registration
gems.what_it_is: Under the Aadhaar (Authentication and Offline Verification) Regulations as amended in 2025, private entities can register as Offline Verification Seeking Entities (OVSE) at ovse.uidai.gov.in. They can then verify Aadhaar verifiable credentials shared from the new Aadhaar App, with selective disclosure and offline face verification for proof of presence. Integration is via QR, app-to-app intent or web-to-app with a callback URL. UIDAI publishes an OVSE handbook and a list of registered entities.
gems.why_gem: It is new (rolled out early 2026; UIDAI reported 100+ entities onboarded by about Apr 2026) and consent-based. It lets POOL verify a seller-owner's identity and liveness without storing Aadhaar numbers or photocopies, which reduces DPDP exposure. Most startups still ask sellers to upload an Aadhaar photo.
gems.use_in_pool: The seller owner shares only name, photo and verified status from their Aadhaar App, with a face check, during onboarding. Optionally, at high-value pickups, the buyer shows a selective credential or face match as proof of presence alongside the delivery code.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Aadhaar photocopy or OCR uploads, and complements DigiLocker KYC through Cashfree.
gems.license_or_pricing: Government framework. No fee is stated on the OVSE page. It requires POOL's Pvt Ltd to apply, which the founder must do.
gems.activity_evidence: UIDAI OVSE page is live today. The UIDAI press note says 100 entities onboarded within 3 months of rollout. ETV Bharat reported the same in April 2026.
gems.maturity_risk: Medium to high. Approval is needed and no sandbox is mentioned. How many buyers and sellers have installed the new Aadhaar App is unknown. Not required for the investor prototype.

gems.name: ONDC logistics and network access via Beckn-ONIX plus ONDC's TypeScript mock playground
gems.what_it_is: Beckn-ONIX is the protocol middleware adapter (Go, rewritten with a plugin framework in Aug 2025) that sits between a buyer app (BAP) or seller app (BPP) and a Beckn/ONDC network, handling signing, validation and routing. ONDC-Official has recently published TypeScript tooling: automation-mock-playground-service (created Feb 2026, simulates ONDC buyer and seller flows) and automation-mcp (an MCP server created Jul 2026). ONDC logistics now includes Uber Direct (live in Bengaluru since about Dec 2025), Shadowfax, Pidge, Loadshare and Zypp.

But ONDC logistics is quietly becoming a one-integration route to many fleets, including Uber's. The tooling to integrate is now far better than the 2023 reputation: an actively maintained adapter pushed today and a TS mock playground.
gems.use_in_pool: Not in the prototype. After the pilot, POOL can register as a logistics buyer app to get quotes from several fleets in one call, and later as a retail buyer app to route pooled demand to ONDC sellers. It also serves as an investor slide: 'plugs into India's public commerce rails'.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Later, it can add to or replace single-courier integrations (Borzo or Porter) with network-wide logistics quotes.
gems.license_or_pricing: Beckn-ONIX is MIT (LICENSE file; the README badge says Apache-2.0 and is stale). ONDC participation needs network-participant registration and compliance testing (Pramaan); network fees were not verified.
gems.activity_evidence: beckn-onix: 99 stars, last push 30 Sep 2026. ONDC-Official org repos pushed 24-30 Sep 2026 (automation-*, mobility, FIS specs). developer-docs was pushed 29 Jul 2026.
gems.maturity_risk: High for the prototype timeline because onboarding and certification are heavy. The Uber Direct city list beyond Bengaluru is unverified. The adapter is Go, not TS.

gems.name: WhatsApp Cloud API Groups API
gems.what_it_is: Lets a Cloud API business number create and manage WhatsApp groups programmatically: create, list and update groups; send text, media and template messages into a group; generate and reset invite links; approve or reject join requests; remove participants; and receive 4 group webhooks. Limits: max 8 participants per group, 10,000 groups per business number, one Cloud API business per group, no add-participant endpoint (invite link only), and no interactive messages, calling or disappearing messages.
gems.why_gem: It's new and little known, and 'pool = WhatsApp group' is the obvious India-native mental model. The important verified fact is that it is capped at 8 participants and needs an Official Business Account (green tick), so it cannot hold a public 40-buyer pool. Knowing this now prevents a wrong architecture.

gems.maturity_risk: High for POOL's core use: the 8-member cap and the OBA requirement, which new startups rarely get quickly.

gems.name: Cashfree OneEscrow (regulated escrow with virtual accounts)
gems.what_it_is: A bank escrow account opened through Cashfree with a partner bank and overseen by SEBI-registered trustees. APIs create virtual accounts, allocate funds, transfer between virtual accounts, fetch statements and pay out. The marketplace use case is to hold buyer funds until the buyer confirms receipt.
gems.why_gem: It is the formal, trustee-backed version of 'money held until delivery code'. It becomes relevant if POOL outgrows a PA's settlement-hold feature, for example for large-ticket pools above the Rs 10,000 Reserve Pay cap, or multi-week delivery windows where investors and regulators want a named escrow per pool.
gems.use_in_pool: Later stage: one virtual account per large pool (appliance or builder-material pools). Allocate on payment, release to the seller's virtual account on delivery code, and return the remainder to buyers. The per-pool statement doubles as an audit trail for investors.
gems.replaces_or_adds: It could replace the PA's split-settlement hold for high-value pools. Not needed for the prototype.
gems.license_or_pricing: Commercial. Pricing not published; onboarding is through a support form. It needs a bank escrow agreement and a trustee.
gems.activity_evidence: Docs and API reference (v1) are live today, and the Payouts changelog mentions escrow virtual-account management.
gems.maturity_risk: High setup cost and legal work. Under RBI's PA Master Direction (15 Sep 2025), DvP funds already flow through the PA's escrow, so the simpler route is to use the PA. Only move to this with legal advice.

gems.name: TypeScript 7.0 (native Go compiler, same `tsc` / `typescript` package)
gems.what_it_is: The official TypeScript compiler, rewritten in Go. It is still the `typescript` npm package and the `tsc` command. The team reports 8-12x faster full builds and 6-26% less memory. New defaults: strict on, module esnext, types [].
gems.why_gem: Most teams still think of the native compiler as a preview (`tsgo`). It went stable on 2026-07-08; npm latest is typescript 7.0.2, Apache-2.0. Next.js 16.3 (latest 16.3.7, 2026-09-29) supports it in `next build` through `experimental.useTypeScriptCli: true`. On 5 Windows laptops with a large monorepo, faster type-checks and a faster editor language server are the biggest everyday time saver. Caveat: 7.0 ships without a programmatic API (a new API is promised for 7.1). API-dependent tools must use the side-by-side `@typescript/typescript6` package (6.0.2).
gems.use_in_pool: Start the monorepo on TS 7: `tsc -b --noEmit` in CI and pre-push, and turn on `useTypeScriptCli` in the Next.js 16.3 buyer/seller app. Its strict defaults suit money code (paise/cent amounts, pool states, bid types). Use `@typescript/typescript6` only for a tool that still needs the old API.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces TypeScript 5.x/6.x tsc and the @typescript/native-preview package. Pairs with Oxlint type-aware linting, which is built on the same Go compiler, so no typescript-eslint is needed.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free
gems.activity_evidence: npm typescript 7.0.2 published 2026-07-08; the old microsoft/typescript-go repo (26.2k stars) is now archived because the port merged into mainline; HN 'TypeScript 7' 720 points / 301 comments; @typescript/native-preview had about 8.5M weekly downloads before GA (InfoQ).
gems.maturity_risk: Low for type-checking. Medium for tooling: any tool that calls the TS JS API (ts-morph, some codegen, older lint plugins) must use the typescript6 compat package until 7.1. `next build` type errors lose Next-specific code frames under the CLI mode.

gems.name: Oxlint 1.x with stable type-aware linting (oxlint-tsgolint 7) + Oxfmt
gems.what_it_is: A Rust linter with native React, react-hooks, Next.js, jsx-a11y, import, promise, unicorn and vitest rule sets. Type-aware rules come from tsgolint, which is built on TypeScript 7's Go compiler. Oxfmt is the matching Prettier-compatible formatter.
gems.why_gem: Type-aware linting became stable on 2026-07-22. It covers 59 of typescript-eslint's 61 type-aware rules, including the ones that catch real money bugs: no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises and strict-boolean-expressions. Oxc benchmarks report 12-18x faster than ESLint + typescript-eslint. Most teams still run slow ESLint type-aware configs, or skip them because they are slow. Oxc is part of VoidZero, which Cloudflare acquired on 2026-06-04, with the MIT licence kept.
gems.use_in_pool: One `oxlint --type-aware` run on every save/commit across the web app, API, workers and MCP server. It catches un-awaited promises in payment webhooks (Razorpay/Stripe), hold/release and Wave Drop refund jobs, and jsx-a11y issues on low-end Android screens. Oxfmt keeps diffs clean for the 5 developers and for AI agents.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces ESLint 9 + typescript-eslint + eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y + Prettier. Keep eslint-plugin-i18next's no-literal-string (from the UI research) through Oxlint JS plugins, which were alpha as of 2026-03, or a tiny ESLint run for that one rule until verified.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: oxc-project/oxc 22.9k stars, pushed 2026-09-30; npm oxlint 1.86.0 (2026-09-28), oxfmt 0.71.0 (2026-09-28), oxlint-tsgolint 7.0.2003 (2026-09-24); InfoQ coverage 2026-09.
gems.maturity_risk: Oxlint core and type-aware linting are stable. Oxfmt is still 0.x, so pin its version. The JS-plugin (ESLint plugin) bridge is newer, so check each custom rule.

gems.name: Vite+ 1.0 (`vp` unified toolchain: cached monorepo task runner + check + test + hooks + Node manager)
gems.what_it_is: One MIT CLI that bundles Vite 8 (Rolldown), Vitest 5, Oxlint, Oxfmt, tsdown and Vite Task. Commands: vp run (monorepo tasks, cached from the files, args and env vars each task actually used), vp check (format + lint + typecheck), vp test, vp pack, vp staged / vp hooks (git hooks), vp env (Node version management) and vp install.
gems.why_gem: It was announced as a paid product in 2025, open-sourced as an MIT alpha in March 2026, and reached 1.0 on 2026-09-28. One tool replaces the usual Turborepo + lint-staged + husky + nvm-windows + ESLint + Prettier + Jest stack that 5 people on Windows would otherwise have to keep in sync. It has a PowerShell installer (`irm https://vite.plus/ps1 | iex`), which matters on POOL's Windows machines. Vitest 5 inside it adds a browser-mode trace viewer, `vi.when`, and failures on un-awaited async assertions.
gems.use_in_pool: `vp run build/test/check` from the monorepo root with caching, so CI re-runs only changed packages (web, api, workers, shared domain). `vp staged` runs Oxlint/Oxfmt on staged files before each commit. `vp env` pins the same Node on all 5 laptops. `vp test` runs Vitest 5 unit and browser-mode component tests (price cards, countdown, Telugu/Hindi layouts). The Next.js app keeps `next dev`/`next build`, called as ordinary `vp run` scripts.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Turborepo/Nx, husky + lint-staged (or lefthook), nvm-windows/volta, and separate ESLint/Prettier/Jest configs.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: voidzero-dev/vite-plus 5.9k stars, created 2025-03, pushed 2026-09-30; npm vite-plus 1.0.0 published 2026-09-28; HN 'Vite+ Beta' 234 pts / 153 comments (2026-07-02); vitest 5.0.2 on npm (2026-09-25).
gems.maturity_risk: 1.0 is two days old. The docs do not cover a Next.js (Turbopack) app beyond running its scripts. The Windows setup .exe is not yet code-signed (SmartScreen warning). A team can adopt it piece by piece (vp run + vp check first) and fall back to plain pnpm scripts.

gems.name: Playwright 1.56-1.63 agent features (Test Agents: planner/generator/healer; --debug=cli; `playwright trace` CLI; test locks; isolated retries)
gems.what_it_is: New features built into Playwright Test. `npx playwright init-agents --loop=claude` installs planner, generator and healer agent definitions for Claude Code: the planner explores the app and writes a Markdown test plan, the generator turns it into tests, and the healer repairs failing ones. Also new: a CLI debugger and trace analysis designed for coding agents (1.59), test locks for shared resources (1.63), `retryStrategy: 'isolated'` (1.62), and aria/screen snapshots in traces (1.63).
gems.why_gem: POOL already picked Playwright for E2E and screenshots. What is new is that agent test-writing and self-healing are now part of the free test runner, not a paid platform. For a 5-person team that already uses Claude Code, this turns 'we have no time to write E2E tests' into a planner-to-generator loop per flow. Test locks fit POOL well: several workers can hit one Razorpay/Stripe test-mode sandbox pool without clashing.
gems.use_in_pool: Planner writes Markdown plans for the golden flows: paste link -> confirm product -> join pool -> seller bids -> accept -> test-mode pay -> pickup code -> Wave Drop partial refund. Generator writes the specs, and healer fixes selectors after UI changes. Test locks serialise tests that touch the same test-mode account or pool, and `npx playwright trace` lets Claude read CI failures.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds to the existing Playwright choice. It replaces paid AI-QA SaaS (for example TesterArmy or Momentic-style tools) for the prototype.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free
gems.activity_evidence: microsoft/playwright 96.9k stars, pushed 2026-09-30; @playwright/test 1.63.0 on npm (2026-09-04); State of JS 2025: Playwright satisfaction 91% vs Cypress 72% (secondary summary).
gems.maturity_risk: Low for the runner. Agent output quality depends on the model and needs human review, and the generated tests should stay in the repo as ordinary code. The agent loop spends Claude tokens.

gems.name: fast-check 4 (property-based testing)
gems.what_it_is: A TypeScript property-based testing library with shrinking. It generates thousands of random inputs (amounts, buyer counts, bid ladders, timestamps) and reduces any failure to the smallest failing case. It works inside Vitest.
gems.why_gem: Teams rarely use it, but POOL's core risk is arithmetic and state-machine correctness, not UI. Example tests miss edge cases such as a Wave Drop refund at pool close with 1 vs 37 buyers, uneven paise splits, a seller's guaranteed per-buyer price, or a buyer walking away mid-close. Properties like 'sum of refunds + seller payout + fee == captured amount, to the paise' and 'no buyer ever pays more than their accepted guaranteed price' are exactly what investors and auditors care about.
gems.use_in_pool: Property tests on the pricing/refund engine (INR paise, USD cents), sealed-bid ranking, pool closing-time logic across IST/US time zones, and the order-state machine (held -> released on code -> refunded). Model-based testing (fc.commands) can drive the pool state machine against the real Postgres through PGlite.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a correctness layer that example-based Vitest tests do not give.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: dubzzz/fast-check 5.2k stars, pushed 2026-09-30; npm fast-check 4.10.2 published 2026-09-19.
gems.maturity_risk: Low: a mature library, active since 2017. The learning curve is writing good properties, and Claude can help draft them.

gems.name: Knip 6 (unused files / exports / dependencies finder)
gems.what_it_is: A static analyser that finds unused files, exports, types and npm dependencies (and missing ones) across pnpm workspaces. It has 150+ framework plugins (Next.js, Vitest, Playwright, GitHub Actions), `--fix` autofix, and now an MCP server plus a VS Code extension.
gems.why_gem: With 5 developers plus AI agents generating code fast, dead code and unused dependencies pile up, and every unused dependency is supply-chain attack surface. Knip is the only tool that understands framework entry points (Next.js app router files, Playwright configs) well enough to be low-noise. Its 2026 MCP integration lets Claude Code clean up after itself.
gems.use_in_pool: `knip` in CI on every PR (fail on new unused dependencies/exports), plus a weekly `knip --fix` cleanup. It keeps the shared domain package lean and removes abandoned experiments before investor demos.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces depcheck, ts-prune and unimported (all older or unmaintained).
gems.license_or_pricing: ISC, free
gems.activity_evidence: webpro-nl/knip 12.4k stars, pushed 2026-09-29; npm knip 6.38.0 (2026-09-23); knip.dev claims 40M downloads/month and 15k+ public projects.
gems.maturity_risk: Low. Occasional false positives are handled with config ignores.

gems.name: pnpm 11/12 supply-chain defaults (minimumReleaseAge = 24h by default, blockExoticSubdeps = true, opt-in trustPolicy)
gems.what_it_is: Package-manager settings that block installing any package version published less than 24 hours ago (minimumReleaseAge 1440, default since v11) and block transitive git/tarball ('exotic') dependencies (default true). An opt-in trustPolicy blocks versions whose publisher trust level dropped.
gems.why_gem: This is a 2025-2026 change most people have not caught up with. The 24-hour quarantine directly defeats the npm worm pattern: Shai-Hulud 2.0 (Nov 2025, about 12h to takedown) and the 2026-05 'Mini Shai-Hulud' TanStack wave (about 3h) both used freshly published malicious versions (incident timings from secondary sources). It is a config default, not a new tool, and it protects developer laptops that hold Razorpay/Stripe test keys and cloud credentials.
gems.use_in_pool: Standardise on pnpm 12 (or whichever pnpm version Vite+ drives). Keep minimumReleaseAge at 1440 or more and turn on `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` in pnpm-workspace.yaml. Use minimumReleaseAgeExclude only for urgent security patches. Use pnpm catalogs to pin one version of each shared dependency across apps.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces npm 11 as the workspace package manager (the machine currently has only npm 11). Adds an install-time supply-chain gate.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free

gems.name: Socket Firewall Free (`sfw`)
gems.what_it_is: A zero-config CLI wrapper (`sfw pnpm install`) that runs a short-lived local proxy and checks every package, including transitive ones, against Socket's malware database before it is downloaded. It blocks confirmed (human-reviewed) malware and warns on AI-flagged packages.
gems.why_gem: Launched free in late 2025 with no account or API key and native Windows x64/ARM64 binaries. It complements pnpm's time-based quarantine with content-based blocking, so together they cover both 'too new' and 'known bad'. A GitHub Action (`socketdev/action@v1`, mode: firewall) gives the same protection in CI.
gems.use_in_pool: Every developer and CI job installs through `sfw pnpm install`. This matters because POOL's machines hold payment test keys, WhatsApp Cloud API tokens and Anthropic API keys.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds malware blocking at install time. Replaces nothing POOL currently has; a cheap alternative to paid Snyk/Socket Enterprise.
gems.license_or_pricing: Free. The firewall is under PolyForm Shield 1.0.0 (the npm installer package `sfw` is MIT). Telemetry is mandatory (machine ID, package info, GitHub org names).
gems.activity_evidence: npm sfw 2.0.6 (2026-05-22); Socket CLI @socketsecurity/cli 1.4.0 (2026-09-29); covered by The Register 2025-09-30.
gems.maturity_risk: Low-medium: it needs network access, has no allow-list, does not support private registries, and blocks only confirmed malware. The telemetry must be accepted. Not OSI open source.

gems.name: zizmor (static security analyser for GitHub Actions)
gems.what_it_is: A Rust CLI and GitHub Action that audits workflow YAML for template injection, dangerous pull_request_target use, excessive GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, unpinned or impostor actions, cache poisoning and credential persistence. It also covers Dependabot and pre-commit configs, with SARIF output and `--fix` autofixes.
gems.why_gem: CI is now the favourite attack path: the tj-actions compromise in 2025, and a trivy-action pull_request_target misconfiguration that leaked org secrets in 2026-03 (per Trail of Bits). Trail of Bits hardened zizmor in 2026, including full YAML-anchor support. It is small, fast, MIT and ships a Windows binary. Almost no small startup runs it.
gems.use_in_pool: Run zizmor on .github/workflows in every PR, blocking on high findings. This protects the deploy tokens (Vercel, AWS ap-south-1), payment test keys and the WhatsApp/SMS credentials stored as GitHub secrets. It also enforces SHA-pinned actions and least-privilege `permissions:`.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds workflow security linting, which POOL does not have today.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: zizmorcore/zizmor 6.6k stars, pushed 2026-09-30; release v1.30.1 on 2026-09-09 with a Windows x86_64 binary; Trail of Bits blog 2026-05-22.
gems.maturity_risk: Low. Some pedantic findings need tuning in the config.

gems.name: Betterleaks (secret scanner, successor to Gitleaks)
gems.what_it_is: A Go secrets scanner for repos, files and git history, by Gitleaks' original author (Zach Rice, backed by Aikido Security). It uses BPE-token-efficiency detection instead of entropy (98.6% vs 70.4% recall on CredData, per the project and press), optional live validation of found keys through CEL/Expr rules, and pre-commit hooks.
gems.why_gem: Launched 2026-03-15; most teams still run Gitleaks or nothing. Validation tells you whether a leaked Razorpay/Stripe/Meta key is actually live, which removes false-positive noise. MIT, a pure Go binary with Windows x64/ARM64 zips, and a GHCR container.
gems.use_in_pool: A pre-commit hook on all 5 Windows laptops plus a CI full-history scan. Custom rules cover Razorpay key_id/secret, Cashfree, Stripe rk_/sk_, Meta WhatsApp tokens, MSG91/DLT keys and Anthropic keys.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Gitleaks/TruffleHog; adds commit-time secret blocking.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free

gems.name: Varlock (schema-driven .env with types, validation, redaction and secret-manager plugins)
gems.what_it_is: A drop-in dotenv replacement. A `.env.schema` file (built on the open @env-spec format) declares every variable's type, whether it is sensitive, and which environment it belongs to. Varlock generates TypeScript types, validates at boot, redacts sensitive values from logs and console output, scans for leaks (`varlock scan`), and pulls secrets from 1Password, Infisical, AWS/Azure/GCP secret managers or Bitwarden. It also has a credential-proxy mode that keeps real secret values away from AI coding agents.
gems.why_gem: It is newer (repo created 2025-04) and fits POOL's exact risk better than full vault platforms. POOL has dozens of India/US keys (Razorpay test/live, Stripe, Meta WhatsApp, SMS DLT, Sarvam, Voyage, Anthropic, SerpApi), and developers use Claude Code, which can read .env files. A committed, typed schema means a missing or misnamed key fails at startup, not during an investor demo. Windows is supported through a native helper (@varlock/native-helper-win32-x64).
gems.use_in_pool: One `.env.schema` in the monorepo shared by web, API and workers. Values come from a shared 1Password or Infisical vault, so no one pastes keys in WhatsApp. Sensitive values are redacted in logs, which also helps DPDP. The agent credential proxy keeps live keys out of Claude Code sessions.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces dotenv, t3-env/zod env validation and ad-hoc .env sharing. Can sit in front of Infisical/Doppler/1Password instead of replacing them.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free
gems.activity_evidence: dmno-dev/varlock 4.6k stars, pushed 2026-09-30; npm varlock 1.21.1 published 2026-09-29 (Windows native helper released the same day); Syntax.fm episode 985 (2026-03); HN launch thread 2025-07.
gems.maturity_risk: Medium: a younger project with a small team (dmno-dev). The @env-spec format is theirs. Next.js integration is claimed on the site but not yet tested by us.

gems.name: Bugsink (self-hosted, Sentry-SDK-compatible error tracking)
gems.what_it_is: A single-container error tracker. You point the standard @sentry/nextjs and @sentry/node SDKs at a Bugsink DSN and get stack traces, breadcrumbs, local variables and releases, without Sentry's multi-container self-host stack. It deliberately leaves out session replay and APM.
gems.why_gem: The stack research found Sentry SaaS is US/EU-only and said not to send transaction PII there. Bugsink lets POOL keep the Sentry SDKs but hold India error data in AWS ap-south-1 on one small VM, which helps with DPDP. The HN thread 'I gave up on self-hosted Sentry' (186 pts) shows why the obvious alternative, self-hosted Sentry, is painful. The hosted free tier (15k events/month, 1 user) can also cover early demos.
gems.use_in_pool: India environment: Bugsink in ap-south-1 receives errors from the Next.js app, API, payment-webhook workers and the WhatsApp bot. US environment: Sentry SaaS or a second Bugsink. Same SDK code, only the DSN changes per region.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces self-hosted Sentry / GlitchTip for India data residency. Can complement Sentry SaaS for the US.
gems.license_or_pricing: PolyForm Shield 1.0.0 (source-available, not OSI; free to self-host for internal use, no competing products). Hosted: free 15k events/month (1 user), paid about €16-€158/month for 75k-3M events.
gems.activity_evidence: bugsink/bugsink 2.1k stars, pushed 2026-09-25; release 2.6.1 on 2026-09-25; HN 'I gave up on self-hosted Sentry' 186 pts / 150 comments (2025-04).
gems.maturity_risk: Medium: a small vendor, a source-available licence, and no replay or performance tracing (PostHog covers replay). It needs Docker on a server; Docker on the dev laptops is not required.

gems.name: Claude Code GitHub Action v1 (anthropics/claude-code-action)
gems.what_it_is: An official MIT GitHub Action. It runs Claude Code on your own runner to review PRs automatically (custom checklists, path-specific reviews, OWASP-style security passes) and to respond to `@claude` in PR/issue comments by answering or pushing fixes. Auth options: Anthropic API key, a Claude subscription OAuth token, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry.
gems.why_gem: POOL is already committed to Claude through Anthropic's official channels. This gives AI PR review with no per-seat SaaS fee. Verified 2026 pricing for the alternatives: CodeRabbit $24-30 per developer per month (only a 14-day trial for private repos) and cubic $40 per developer per month. Reviews can encode POOL-specific rules ('never capture before pickup code', 'amounts must be integer paise', 'no PII to US services').
gems.use_in_pool: Auto-review every PR with a POOL checklist: money invariants, RBI/Stripe hold rules, DPDP PII handling, i18n (no hard-coded English strings), and low-end Android bundle size. Engineers use `@claude` to fix review comments. It runs on the same CI runners, and the prompts live in the repo.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces CodeRabbit, cubic and Greptile seats. Adds automated review for a 5-person team with no dedicated reviewer.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT action. You pay Claude API tokens per review (cost per review not verified; Opus 5.5 is $4/$20 per million tokens per the project notes, so use Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 4.5 for routine reviews to cut cost) or use a Claude subscription token.
gems.activity_evidence: anthropics/claude-code-action 9.2k stars, created 2025-05, pushed 2026-09-30; v1 tag (2025-08-26) with ongoing updates.

gems.name: Grafana k6 v2 (load testing with native TypeScript)
gems.what_it_is: A Go load-testing engine that runs .ts scripts directly (esbuild type-stripping, on by default since v0.57). It supports scenarios, thresholds and a browser module. v2.3.0 added `--scenario` to run one workload and `--once` to reuse load scripts as smoke/functional tests.
gems.why_gem: k6 is well known, but two 2025-2026 changes make it fit a TypeScript team well: scripts are plain TS in the monorepo (no bundling), and `--once` turns the same script into a post-deploy smoke test. POOL's hardest traffic shape, a burst of joins and payments right before a buyer-chosen pool closing time plus the Wave Drop refund fan-out, needs a real load test before an investor live demo.
gems.use_in_pool: Scenarios: 500 buyers joining one mutton or electronics pool in the last 60 seconds; concurrent sealed bids; a payment-webhook storm (Razorpay/Stripe test mode, or a mocked webhook sender); refund fan-out at close. The same script with `--once` runs as a smoke check after every deploy.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds load and smoke testing. Replaces Artillery, JMeter and ad-hoc scripts.
gems.license_or_pricing: AGPL-3.0 (fine as an internal test tool that is never shipped or offered as a service; this matches the project rule of no AGPL in core). Grafana Cloud k6 has a free tier (limits not verified here).
gems.activity_evidence: grafana/k6 31.7k stars, pushed 2026-09-29; release v2.3.0 on 2026-09-21.
gems.maturity_risk: Low. TS support strips types but does not type-check; run tsc separately. Do not load-test real Razorpay/Stripe endpoints beyond their test-mode rate limits.

gems.name: Blacksmith (drop-in faster GitHub Actions runners)
gems.what_it_is: Managed GitHub Actions runners, used by changing the `runs-on:` label. Faster hardware and cache downloads, optional Docker-layer caching and sticky disks. Linux, Windows and macOS runners.

Blacksmith's verified pricing: 3,000 free minutes per month with no credit card, then $0.004/min for Linux x64 2 vCPU (their claim: 33% cheaper per minute and about 2x faster than GitHub-hosted). gems.use_in_pool: Run the Playwright and Vitest browser jobs on Blacksmith runners with sticky-disk caching of the pnpm store and Playwright browsers. Keep light jobs (zizmor, Betterleaks, Oxlint) on GitHub-hosted runners.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces GitHub-hosted runners for heavy jobs. An alternative to Depot, Namespace or self-hosted runners.
