gems.name: Takumi (takumi-js / @takumi-rs/core)
gems.what_it_is: A Rust engine that renders JSX, HTML and CSS (Tailwind-style `tw` props) into PNG, WebP or JPEG images, animations and paged PDFs without a headless browser. It uses the parley text-layout library for text shaping.
gems.why_gem: Most POOL growth happens through a link pasted into WhatsApp, and WhatsApp shows only the og:image and title. A live share card per pool ('7 joined, price now Rs 61,400, closes 8 pm') is the viral loop. The obvious choice is Satori/@vercel/og. Satori only switched to HarfBuzz shaping in 0.33, and that version has open bundling issues: #791, where hb.wasm fails to resolve under Next.js/Turbopack, and #802, where WOFF glyphs render as bars. Its ICU4X Unicode tracking issue #743 is still open. Takumi is one native call, ships prebuilt win32-x64 binaries (good for the 5 Windows devs), and the same component also produces PDF receipts and handover slips.
gems.use_in_pool: GET /og/pool/:id returns a 1200x630 WebP of the live pool state in Telugu, Hindi or English, cached for a short time and busted on every join or bid. The same JSX template, through takumi-pdf, renders the buyer's receipt and the dealer's pickup slip.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Satori/@vercel/og (or a Puppeteer screenshot service) for OG images. Adds PDF receipts with no Chromium.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (npm), free
gems.activity_evidence: 3,057 GitHub stars, created 2025-06-01, pushed 2026-09-30. takumi@2.14.0 released 2026-09-15. @takumi-rs/core has about 419k npm downloads a week and takumi-js about 285k (week of 22-28 Sep 2026).
gems.maturity_risk: Single maintainer project. Telugu conjunct rendering is not verified: parley does shaping, but render a Telugu and Devanagari test card before committing. CSS support is a subset of the browser's.

gems.name: Chatwoot v4.13-v4.18 (2026 WhatsApp upgrades)
gems.what_it_is: The open-source omnichannel helpdesk POOL already chose for its ops team. It is included here because its 2026 releases changed what it can do on WhatsApp.
gems.why_gem: The release notes for v4.13.0 (2026-04-17) through v4.18.0 (2026-09-18) add these features: support for WhatsApp BSUIDs (business-scoped user IDs, Meta's 2026 change); WhatsApp and Twilio calling, with a voice-call dashboard and WhatsApp voice messages; WhatsApp coexistence fixes; Click-to-WhatsApp referral and WhatsApp Flow responses shown inside the conversation; guided WhatsApp setup and account-health monitoring; and Cloud API template management through the API. So a buyer who taps 'Call support' in WhatsApp can reach an agent without a phone line, and a support agent can see which Flow the buyer filled in. The Captain AI features are marked [Enterprise]. The WhatsApp and calling items are not.
gems.use_in_pool: One inbox for 4 ops staff covering buyer disputes, 'dealer did not show', and handover-code problems. WhatsApp voice calls go to the same agent. The conversation shows the Flow response (for example 'report an issue with order #') and the referral ad or source.
gems.replaces_or_adds: No change to the stack choice. It removes the need for a separate calling tool (Exotel, Twilio Voice) for WhatsApp support in the prototype.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT outside the enterprise/ directory (Captain AI is Enterprise). Free to self-host.
gems.activity_evidence: 37,356 stars, pushed 2026-09-30, v4.18.0 released 2026-09-18, monthly releases since April 2026
gems.maturity_risk: Ruby/Rails with Sidekiq and Redis, so a stack the TypeScript team does not know. The team uses it only through its API and webhooks. WhatsApp calling needs Meta's calling enablement on the number.

gems.name: GrowthBook 5.0 (warehouse-native experiments on POOL's own Postgres)
gems.what_it_is: An open-source feature-flag and experimentation platform that computes experiment results by running SQL against your own database or warehouse.
gems.why_gem: PostHog experiments measure PostHog events. POOL's real outcome metrics live in its own Postgres ledger: accepted bids, paid bookings, Wave Drop refunds, completed handover codes. GrowthBook supports Postgres as a data source (per its docs) and analyses those ground-truth tables directly. v4.0 (2025-07-09) added Safe Rollouts with auto-rollback, custom decision criteria and an MCP server. v5.0 (2026-07-20) added official agent Skills, a CLI with full REST coverage, JSON-schema validation of flag values, 'Configs' for typed remote config, and unreachable-rule detection. The pricing page lists CUPED and sequential testing on Pro, which matters for POOL's small traffic.
gems.use_in_pool: Test Wave Drop slab presentation, booking-amount size, and default closing-time suggestions. Measure them on paid-and-handed-over orders from Postgres, not on clicks. Safe Rollouts with auto-rollback for risky flow changes (for example the new bid-reveal screen).
gems.replaces_or_adds: Upgrades the 'GrowthBook as alternative' line in the stack to the experiment-analysis layer. PostHog stays for funnels and replay.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT outside enterprise directories. Cloud Starter is free (3 users, unlimited flags and experiments, 1M CDN requests a month). Pro is $40 per seat per month (includes CUPED, sequential testing, bandits). Self-hosting the open-source version is free.
gems.maturity_risk: Low. It is well established. Sequential testing and CUPED may be paid features. Whether they are in the open-source self-hosted version is not verified.

gems.name: PostHog Workflows (GA 30 Dec 2025)
gems.what_it_is: Event-triggered messaging automation built into PostHog. Workflows send email, SMS (Twilio), mobile push (FCM and APNs, open beta), Slack and CDP destinations. Triggers include product events, cohort changes and feature-flag or experiment exposure.
gems.why_gem: Most people think of PostHog as analytics only. Since the GA on 2025-12-30 it can run lifecycle nudges from the same events POOL already tracks, with no Customer.io or Braze sync. The free tier covers 10,000 messages a month across all channels. After that it is from $0.005 per send.
gems.use_in_pool: Growth nudges only, not transactional messages. Examples: 'you pasted a link but did not POOL it' after 24 h; 'your pool is 2 buyers short and closes in 3 h'; US email win-back. It can use experiment variants from the same tool.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds lifecycle marketing without a separate tool. Novu stays for transactional and WhatsApp messages: PostHog Workflows has no WhatsApp channel in its docs.
gems.license_or_pricing: PostHog Cloud: 10k messages a month free, then from $0.005 per send. The main repo is MIT outside ee/.
gems.activity_evidence: GA blog post dated 2025-12-30. The channels docs page lists Email, Slack, Twilio SMS, Push (FCM and APNs, open beta) and CDP. PostHog repo has about 40k stars and is pushed daily.
gems.maturity_risk: No WhatsApp channel, and WhatsApp is POOL's main channel in India. Push is still beta. There is a risk of sending the same nudge twice from both Novu and PostHog: keep one owner per message type.

gems.name: Dub (Dub Links deep links + Dub Partners)
gems.what_it_is: An open-source link-attribution platform: branded short links, conversion tracking, iOS and Android deep links with deferred deep linking (launched 2025-03-27), and Dub Partners for referral and affiliate programs.
gems.why_gem: Firebase Dynamic Links shut down in August 2025, and Branch and AppsFlyer are expensive enterprise products. Dub's documented deferred deep linking uses the Google Install Referrer on Android and a clipboard-or-IP match on iOS, with React Native examples. A pool invite link from WhatsApp can therefore land a new Android user inside the right pool after they install the app. The same system tracks link click → signup → paid booking.
gems.use_in_pool: Every pool gets a branded short link (for example pool.link/abc) that carries the referrer ID. The link opens the app at that pool, or the PWA if the app is not installed. Conversion events (joined, paid, handed over) are attributed to the sharer. Dub Partners is for a later dealer or creator affiliate program.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Firebase Dynamic Links, Branch and a home-made shortener. Adds click-to-purchase attribution.
gems.license_or_pricing: AGPL-3.0 with an ee/ directory under a commercial licence. Dub Links has a free plan, but deep links need Pro or higher (the Pro price was not shown on the pages I fetched). Dub Partners plans are $90/mo (Business) and $300/mo (Advanced), plus a 5% payout fee. There is no free Partners tier.
gems.activity_evidence: 24,846 GitHub stars, pushed 2026-09-30. The deep-links changelog entry is dated 2025-03-27.
gems.maturity_risk: Deep links are a paid feature. Partner payouts to India are not verified. For India, POOL rewards should be POOL credits anyway, not cash payouts. Self-hosting is AGPL. The IP-based iOS matching is probabilistic.

gems.name: LinkForty Core
gems.what_it_is: A self-hosted deep-linking engine on Postgres. It provides device-aware smart links, deferred deep linking through fingerprint matching, click analytics, QR codes, HMAC-signed webhooks and OG preview pages. It has MIT-licensed SDKs for React Native, Expo, iOS, Android and Flutter.
gems.why_gem: It is the only open-source, self-hostable Branch or Firebase Dynamic Links replacement I found that has an Expo SDK. Click data stays in POOL's Mumbai Postgres, which helps DPDP data residency, and there is no per-click fee. Built-in QR codes suit the offline side: meat-shop counters and dealer showrooms.
gems.use_in_pool: This is the self-hosted fallback if Dub's paid deep links or its US-hosted click data do not fit India. Use it for dealer-counter QR posters ('scan to join the Saturday mutton pool') and webhook events into POOL's ledger.
gems.replaces_or_adds: An alternative to Dub for deep links. Replaces Firebase Dynamic Links.
gems.license_or_pricing: Core is AGPL-3.0. The SDKs (mobile-sdk-expo, -react-native, -ios, -android) are MIT. Self-hosting is free.

gems.name: c15t (consent management, v2)
gems.what_it_is: A headless, TypeScript-first consent management platform for React, Next.js and Vue. It includes a banner and preference centre, a self-hostable backend that stores consent records, geo-based jurisdiction policies, IAB TCF, Google Consent Mode v2, and Global Privacy Control.
gems.why_gem: It is newer and much lighter than OneTrust, Cookiebot or CookieYes. The source applies CCPA presets for California regions and honours GPC (`Sec-GPC: 1`), which denies marketing and measurement. That covers the US web side. Consent records are stored in POOL's own database, not a vendor's.
gems.use_in_pool: On POOL's US web app, one consent state gates PostHog replay, marketing pixels and Dub conversion scripts, with GPC honoured. For India, the same headless store can hold per-purpose consent receipts, but a custom policy is needed (see risk).
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces a SaaS cookie CMP. Adds consent receipts to POOL's own database.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0. Self-hosting is free. Hosted pricing on consent.io was not checked.
gems.activity_evidence: 1,920 stars, pushed 2026-09-30. c15t latest is 2.2.1 on npm, with 3.0.0-alpha.3 published 2026-09-28. About 212k npm downloads a week.
gems.maturity_risk: In the source, India (IN) and the US outside CCPA regions map to jurisdiction 'NONE' (no banner), so there is no DPDP policy out of the box. There is no React Native package (@c15t/react-native returns 404). v3 is in alpha, so expect API churn.

gems.name: truConsent (DPDP-native CMP) + truKIT React Native SDK
gems.what_it_is: A consent and privacy-compliance platform built for India's DPDP Act by a Bangalore company (Tangled Threads Technologies, IITM-incubated). It covers the consent lifecycle, a rights centre for access, correction, deletion and nomination, data mapping (truScanner, MIT, on GitHub), and notices in all 22 scheduled languages. India data residency is the default.
gems.why_gem: Global CMPs are built around cookies and GDPR. DPDP needs itemised, purpose-level notices in the user's language (Telugu and Hindi for POOL), withdrawal as easy as giving consent, and DSR handling. The timeline: DPDP Rules notified 13-14 Nov 2025; Consent Manager registration opens around 13 Nov 2026; notice, consent and security obligations apply from 13 May 2027. POOL's pitch can show DPDP-ready consent before competitors.
gems.use_in_pool: An itemised consent notice in Telugu, Hindi or English at phone-OTP signup and on WhatsApp opt-in. A withdraw-consent control. DSR requests (delete my data) handled through a workflow instead of email.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a DPDP-specific consent layer that c15t and Western CMPs do not provide.
gems.license_or_pricing: Proprietary SaaS. Prices are behind an email gate and were not verified. truScanner is MIT. The truKIT-react-native and truKIT-flutter-sdk repos exist, created 2026-09-29.
gems.activity_evidence: The website claims 22-language support and India residency. truscanner has 18 stars (pushed 2026-07-06). The SDK repos have 0 stars and are brand new.
gems.maturity_risk: Early vendor. Pricing is unknown. The SDK is only days old. It is not verified whether the product is a registered Consent Manager or only a CMP. Registration needs ₹2 crore net worth, according to a secondary source.

gems.name: TSI DPDP Consent Management System
gems.what_it_is: An open-source consent management system for India's DPDP Act from TSI Coop. It can be self-hosted by a data fiduciary or run multi-tenant by a Consent Manager. It publishes its system design and a data-lifecycle and erasure design.
gems.why_gem: It is the only open-source DPDP-specific consent data model I found that is actively maintained. It gives POOL a free, citable reference design for consent artifacts, purposes, withdrawal and erasure, instead of inventing one. The only other option is WSO2's heavier dpdp-accelerator, which needs the WSO2 Identity Server.
gems.use_in_pool: Copy its consent-artifact schema and erasure-interface ideas into POOL's own Postgres consent tables (TypeScript). Running the Java service itself is not recommended.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a reference design. It does not replace a runtime component.
gems.license_or_pricing: Apache-2.0, free
gems.activity_evidence: 14 stars, created 2025-07-26, pushed 2026-09-29, binary release v0.5.2
gems.maturity_risk: Java, not TypeScript. Tiny community. Treat it as a design reference only.

gems.name: Libredesk (Zerodha Tech)
gems.what_it_is: A self-hosted customer-support desk shipped as a single Go binary. It handles email, live chat and (from v2.9) WhatsApp through the Meta Cloud API with templates. It has a multilingual help centre, an AI assistant and copilot, SLAs, CSAT, macros, automations, SSO and webhooks.
gems.why_gem: It is an Indian open-source project with a Zerodha Tech badge, and it is far lighter to run than Chatwoot: one binary plus Postgres, with no Rails, Sidekiq or Redis. Built-in CSAT and SLA timers suit POOL's proof-based trust story, and the multilingual help centre suits Telugu and Hindi FAQs.
gems.use_in_pool: A candidate replacement for Chatwoot once v2.9 is stable: a WhatsApp support inbox, SLA alerts on 'handover-code not working' tickets, and CSAT after each resolved dispute.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Could replace Chatwoot and remove the Ruby stack from ops.
gems.license_or_pricing: AGPL-3.0, free to self-host

gems.name: wacrm (CRM template for WhatsApp)
gems.what_it_is: A self-hostable Next.js 16 + Supabase CRM on the official Meta Cloud API. It includes a shared WhatsApp inbox with assignment, contacts with tags and CSV import, Kanban sales pipelines linked to conversations, template broadcasts with delivery and read tracking, a no-code automation builder, a bring-your-own-key AI reply assistant with a knowledge base, team roles and a public REST API.
gems.why_gem: POOL's supply side is dealers and meat shops who live on WhatsApp. The ops team needs a pipeline for recruiting them (lead → docs submitted → KYC → first bid) inside the same WhatsApp thread. It is MIT-licensed and written in TypeScript and React, so the team can fork it. Twenty, the CRM in the current stack, is AGPL and has no native WhatsApp inbox.
gems.use_in_pool: An internal 'Seller Desk': recruit and onboard dealers over WhatsApp, track them in a pipeline, send approved template broadcasts ('new mutton pool in Kukatpally, 40 kg demand, bid by 6 pm'), and let the AI draft replies from the seller FAQ.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces Twenty CRM or a spreadsheet for dealer acquisition. It sits beside Chatwoot, which serves buyers.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free to self-host (it needs Supabase or Postgres)

gems.name: Atomic CRM (marmelab)
gems.what_it_is: A full-featured CRM starter (contacts, companies, deals Kanban, notes, tasks, activity) built with React, shadcn/ui and Supabase, from the makers of react-admin.
gems.why_gem: It uses the same UI language as POOL (shadcn) and is MIT-licensed, so its components can go straight into POOL's seller console. It fits the dealer-facing side: each dealer gets a light CRM of their own POOL buyers, their bids won and lost, and follow-ups. This is something BSP tools like Interakt or Gallabox do not give a marketplace.
gems.use_in_pool: The seller console's 'My customers and deals' tab. A dealer sees repeat buyers from past pools (with consent), bid history and notes. Built by forking its deals Kanban and contact views on top of POOL's own API.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds a seller-side CRM without licensing a SaaS CRM for each dealer.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free

gems.name: WhatsApp Cloud API Groups API
gems.what_it_is: A Meta API that lets a Cloud API business number create invite-only WhatsApp groups, list and update them, and generate or reset invite links. It supports text, media and template messages.
gems.why_gem: It is a community feature that looks built for small pools. A 'society mutton pool' could have its own WhatsApp group run by POOL's number, so neighbours coordinate pickup in the app they already use. The limits are strict (see risk).
gems.use_in_pool: An optional 'pickup group' for tiny local pools (up to 7 buyers plus the POOL number) for pickup-time coordination and a handover photo.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Adds native group chat in WhatsApp, instead of building in-app group chat.

No interactive messages, calling or commerce messages in groups. Prototype value is low until OBA is granted.

gems.name: OfferKit
gems.what_it_is: A self-hosted promotion engine for coupons, gift cards (full ledger), loyalty points, referrals (codes with dual-reward conversions), segments and validation rules. It has a dashboard, REST API, a TypeScript SDK derived from an oRPC contract, a CLI, and an MCP server that tags each tool's risk level.
gems.why_gem: Ethical referrals for POOL mean rewarding only real, completed, handed-over purchases, with capped credits and no cash-for-signups. That needs a proper credit ledger with atomic, idempotent redemption, and OfferKit provides one. It is built on oRPC, the RPC layer already picked in POOL's backend research, and it is MIT with no paywalled features.
gems.use_in_pool: Referral codes where both sides get a POOL credit after the referred buyer's first handover code is entered. Wave Drop or goodwill credits could be issued as ledgered gift-card-like balances with atomic rollback.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces a home-made referral and credits table. It is an alternative to Dub Partners, which is built for cash affiliate payouts.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free to self-host (Postgres + Redis)
gems.activity_evidence: 46 stars, created 2026-05-08, v0.2.0 released 2026-08-18, last commit 2026-08-18
gems.maturity_risk: Very early (v0.2), with no commits for 6 weeks. It is not verified whether it handles INR or multiple currencies in referral rewards. Money-like credits must stay consistent with POOL's pgledger, so keep OfferKit as the rules engine and the ledger as the source of truth.

gems.name: @marinedotsh/better-auth-referral
gems.what_it_is: A Better Auth plugin that gives each user a referral code, records who referred whom at signup (from an x-referral-code header), and exposes typed referral stats. Its configurable multi-step success (for example `steps: ['email_verified','first_purchase']`) sets what counts as a successful referral.
gems.why_gem: POOL already chose Better Auth. The multi-step success is the ethical pattern: a referral counts only after a real purchase, which blocks fake-signup farming. It adds roughly one plugin and one migration instead of a service.
gems.use_in_pool: Referral attribution at signup, with success set to first_purchase, which maps to 'first handover code entered'. Then call OfferKit or POOL's ledger to issue credits.
gems.replaces_or_adds: Replaces hand-rolled referral attribution columns.
gems.license_or_pricing: MIT, free

gems.name: notifkit
gems.what_it_is: A self-hosted TypeScript notification engine on Postgres and Redis. gems.replaces_or_adds: A possible lighter alternative to Novu.

Standards to follow: India's BIS IS 19000:2022 (voluntary; a quality control order was discussed but I could not confirm it is mandatory as of today), and the US FTC rule 16 CFR Part 465 (penalties up to $51,744 per violation per secondary sources). SuprSend (Indian notification infrastructure; free 10k notifications a month; Essentials $110/mo; channels include WhatsApp; SuprSend AI launched on Product Hunt 2026-05-22): verified from its pricing page but not included as a gem, because user preferences are paid-only and Novu already covers this. India DLT SMS handling was not checked.

Sublay (comments, chat, spaces, moderation and reputation bundles; SDKs Apache-2.0; free for 500 MAU, then $15/$25/$75 a month): verified as hosted-only with no self-host option; its data region (India) is not disclosed, so it was left out for DPDP reasons.

Unofficial WhatsApp gateways (OpenWA 14.8k stars, WAHA-based CRMs such as DeskcommCRM): deliberately excluded. They use the unofficial WhatsApp Web protocol and risk number bans. POOL must use the official Cloud API only.
YC W25-F26 batches: my searches did not surface any relevant new company in this area. This is not proof that none exists.

swaps.current_pick: Temporal (pool timers, payout holds) plus pg-boss and Valkey/BullMQ for jobs
swaps.replace_with: DBOS Transact TS (@dbos-inc/dbos-sdk, MIT), pinned to 5.2.x, running in-process on the same Postgres. It ships a Drizzle template. Do not use DBOS Conductor SaaS; self-host it or skip it for India data. Keep Valkey only if a cache is later needed.
swaps.why: Spot-checked on GitHub and npm: MIT, 1,380 stars, v5.0 on 2026-09-16, v5.1 on 09-24, v5.2 on 09-29, npm 5.2.11. It gives durable sleep until the buyer-chosen close, checkpointed steps (capture, then Route transfer on_hold, then Wave Drop refunds), recv/timeouts for the delivery-code wait, rate-limited queues for WhatsApp sends, and exactly-once cron. That removes three moving parts (Temporal cluster or cloud, Redis, a queue library) for 5 Windows developers, and it survives a crash without double refunds.
swaps.risk: Three minor releases in two weeks, so pin exactly and read changelogs before upgrading. DBOS closed its 'PGLite support' issue as not_planned (2026-03-11) and uses LISTEN plus its own connections, so it will NOT run on PGlite. Local dev needs real Postgres (Docker or a per-developer cloud branch). Workflow code must be deterministic, with every side effect in a step. The community is smaller than Temporal's.

swaps.current_pick: US pools longer than about 7 days: charge in full via Stripe Connect, then a Wave Drop partial refund at close
swaps.replace_with: Stripe manual capture with payment_method_options.card.request_extended_authorization=if_available. Capture only the winning per-buyer price with amount_to_capture. Read charge.payment_method_details.card.capture_before to cap each buyer's closing-time picker.
swaps.why: Verified on Stripe's docs today. Mastercard allows 30 days in all categories. Visa allows 29d 18h in all categories, with a +0.08% fee outside lodging and rental. Test cards 4242 and 5555 exercise it in test mode, and the docs say availability in test mirrors live. Networks intend it for cases where the final amount is unknown at authorisation, which is POOL's case. The buyer is never charged and then refunded, so there are fewer disputes and no refund float.
swaps.risk: Needs IC+ pricing, or a support request on blended pricing, before live use. Amex and Discover get extended windows only in travel and lodging, so those cards fall back to a 7-day cap or charge-and-refund. Not available when Link is the payment method type. Holds must use clear statement descriptors. Keep the charge-and-refund path as a fallback.

swaps.current_pick: Meilisearch (separate search service plus sync pipeline)
swaps.replace_with: Postgres-native search for the prototype: tsvector with the 'simple' configuration, pg_trgm for fuzzy and Telugu/Hindi script, and pgvector (Voyage) similarity, fused with reciprocal rank fusion in one SQL query. Consider pg_textsearch BM25 only if the chosen host supports it.
swaps.why: For a prototype catalogue of thousands of products and pools, a second stateful service and a sync pipeline cost more than they return. Everything already lives in Postgres 18 with pgvector. pg_textsearch is real (PostgreSQL licence, v1.4.0 on 2026-08-18) but only runs on Tiger Cloud or self-hosted, so it is not a safe default.
swaps.risk: Relevance tuning and typo tolerance are weaker than Meilisearch's out of the box. Telugu/Hindi quality with 'simple' plus trigram must be tested on real queries. Re-add Meilisearch if search becomes a product surface.

swaps.replace_with: Server-Sent Events through oRPC event iterators, fed by Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY or DBOS events
swaps.why: POOL's live data only flows one way: joins count, countdown, price tier and 'new bid arrived'. SSE runs over plain HTTP, reconnects automatically, passes proxies and CDNs, and needs no sticky sessions or Redis adapter. That is lighter on low-end Android and on ops. oRPC was verified: MIT, @orpc/server 1.15.4 stable on 2026-09-23.
swaps.risk: Buyer-to-buyer chat or seller two-way interaction would need WebSockets later. Some serverless hosts cap long-lived responses, so run SSE from the long-running Node service. Do not use oRPC v2 beta.

additions.what_it_adds: A real double-entry ledger that commits in the same Postgres transaction as order and pool state. Verified in the source: allow_negative_balance and allow_positive_balance checks, plus accounts locked in sorted order with FOR UPDATE to avoid deadlocks. MIT, 494 stars, pushed 2026-09-30. Add POOL's own idempotency-key table, because pgledger has none. Its README roadmap admits there are no numbered upgrade migrations yet, so pin the SQL file.
Typed INR/USD money with allocate(), so Wave Drop rebates and commission splits sum exactly to the paise or cent. It gives compile-time errors on currency mismatch. Verified on npm: 2.0.2, MIT.

Property tests: refunds + seller payout + fee = captured amount, and no buyer ever pays more than the accepted guaranteed price. The same properties cover the pool state machine. This is the evidence of money correctness investors and auditors want.

top_10_for_investor_wow: Paste a real Flipkart or Amazon link: Claude returns the exact product, and every field is shown with the verbatim quote from the source page (verified server-side). Anything it cannot prove is labelled 'unconfirmed' on screen.

Scan the barcode on a real pack with zxing-wasm and get a GTIN-exact match. Two buyers pasting different store links for the same item land in the same pool (Voyage multimodal plus a Claude same/different check).
Hold, don't charge (US): a Stripe test-mode extended authorisation shows as a hold. At close only the lower winning price is captured and the rest releases, visible live in the Stripe dashboard.
A live pool page where the price rolls down with NumberFlow as real joins arrive over SSE, plus a WhatsApp share card (Takumi) that shows the current price and time left, regenerated on every join.
A Telugu voice note on WhatsApp ('rendu kilo mutton curry cut, Sunday') is transcribed by Sarvam Saaras v4 and turned into a pool join by Claude, with a Telugu voice reply from Bulbul v3.
A seller submits a private bid through a WhatsApp Flow without installing an app. The buyer sees the guaranteed per-buyer price and accepts or walks away.

Proof-based delivery: one Borzo sandbox multi-drop order per pool with route optimisation, per-drop photo and signature proof, a DIGIPIN on every address, and a scan of the buyer's QR handover code that releases the Razorpay Route on_hold transfer.

Crash-proof money, shown live: kill the worker process in the middle of a pool close. DBOS resumes from the last checkpoint, and the pgledger trial balance still ties to the paise with Razorpay/Stripe test-mode records, with no double refunds.
A 'Verified seller' badge built from real, dated checks: GSTIN, then penny-drop bank name match against the GST legal name, then FSSAI licence validity for meat shops.
Join a pool from inside Claude through POOL's own MCP server (find_pool, join_pool, pool_status). Payment still completes on POOL's licensed-PA checkout, never inside the chat.
